text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- Yugoslav Deputy Foreign minister Zivadin Jovanovic and Italian deputy Foreign Minister Piero Fassino sign a technical cooperation agreement between the two ministries in Belgrade Monday.
- Serbian parliament to hold its regular session on December 3, the agenda includes discussing the law on labour relations and a bill on pension and disability insurance.
- Moscow plans to build a gas pipeline in Yugoslavia and an oil pipeline from Budapest in Hungary to Novi Sad in Yugoslavia, the Russian ministry for international economic cooperation said.
- World bank delegation visits Yugoslavia for the first time since imposition of sanctions almost five years ago.

- Normalisation of relations with international financial and trade organisations is the key problem for the realisation of aims of Yugoslavia's economic policy according to a government report examined at a meeting of Yugoslav, Serbian and Montenegrin prime ministers.
- General manager of Zrenjanin cooking oil industry Dijamant Savo Knezevic was declared the most successful Yugoslav manager for 1996.
- Serbia plans connecting 17,000 new lines to the GSM network by the end of the year.
- Belgrade food fair to be held from December 11 to 14.
- Belgrade's road institute proposes increase of excise duties on oil derivatives for financing the county's road infrastructure.

- According to unofficial results of the run-off local elections the opposition has won in major Serbian cities Belgrade, Novi Sad, Nis, Kragujevac while the ruling left coalition won in 134 Serbian municipalities.
- Montenegro's new parliament reelects Svetozar Marovic as parliament Speaker at its constituent session Monday.
- Former petrol dealers in Yugoslavia turn to new lucrative business of coffee smuggling, costing the government about 4.5 German marks in unpaid taxes per one kilo of coffee.
- The Serbian oil industry NIS proposes raising the price of oil derivatives by between 10 and 30 percent.
